subject: Clarify derivative outputs / subprocessor flow for DPA — next steps for execution
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@healthcore.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@healthcore.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@healthcore.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T09:03:00Z
Subject: DPA redlines — model training / derivative outputs

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the draft DPA. Attached are HealthCore's redlines (HealthCore_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf). Primary items of concern: 1) explicit prohibition on using HealthCore customer prompts, responses, or PII to train or improve models; 2) clarity on what counts as "Derived Models" and whether those can be shared outside of HealthCore; and 3) a current list of subprocessors and data residency commitments for US-only data.

Suggested high-level language: a clear ban on "training" on Customer Content (we define training as any process that causes persistent model parameter updates attributable to Customer Content), with an exception for ephemeral telemetry used to debug operational issues.

Can Redwood provide an alternate clause that: 1) disallows training on Customer Content; 2) defines any permitted use for improving service quality as aggregated, de-identified telemetry; and 3) gives HealthCore the right to audit or receive an attestation around subprocessor handling?

We'd like to get to an executed DPA via DocuSign in the next 5 business days if possible. Please confirm availability.

Attachments: HealthCore_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf (redlined DPA, PDF)

Sara Klein
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
HealthCore

From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: (internal)
Date: 2027-01-11T10:17:00Z
Subject: FW: DPA redlines — model training / derivative outputs

Karthik / Neha — forwarding HealthCore's redlines and asks. They want an explicit "no training on customer content" clause and a sharp definition of "Derived Models". Also asking for subprocessor list and audit attestation.

Quick asks from me:
- Karthik: can you summarize technical constraints and the minimal language that would allow us to continue service improvement without exposing customer prompts to training? I think we can offer aggregated telemetry and opt-in model improvement, but provide exact wording or bullets we can share.
- Neha: legal POV — are we able to accept an explicit training ban plus an audit attestation? Any redline suggestions for a middle-ground clause that protects HealthCore while keeping product telemetry usable?

I'm attaching an internal snippet (rwd_internal_dpa_snippet.txt) with a draft we used with another enterprise that allowed narrowly scoped service-quality improvements. Please add comments.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T12:04:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: DPA redlines — model training / derivative outputs

Aisha — quick technical rundown and a proposed language fragment.

Technical notes (short):
- Our standard inference stack never persists raw customer prompt/response pairs into long-term training datasets by default. We use a combination of ephemeral KV caches, bounded logs, and privacy filters.
- We perform two classes of improvements: (1) offline model training on curated datasets (requires opt-in / contractual permission), and (2) runtime service improvements (metric-driven tuning, anomaly detection).
- Runtime logs include latencies, error traces, and anonymized feature counters. Any collection that could contain user text is redacted/hashed before being used in automated pipelines.

Proposed language (one-paragraph):
"Provider shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or update model parameters used by Provider for serving models ("Training"). Provider may process aggregated and de-identified telemetry solely to improve service reliability and operational performance ("Service Improvement"). Aggregated and de-identified telemetry excludes Customer Content and does not permit reconstruction of customer prompts or outputs. Model training for the purpose of improving model capabilities, quality, or feature expansion may only occur with Customer's prior written consent and subject to mutually-agreed scope and safeguards."

Subprocessor flow: we can provide a current list and a monthly update cadence. For HealthCore (US-only requirement) we can propose to restrict processing to US regions and to terminate transfer to non-US subprocessors unless explicitly approved. That will require operations to pin the workload to US-only clusters.

Attachments: I saved a short markup (rwd_redline_proposal.docx) with the paragraph above plus an alternate two-sentence variant.

If that language looks OK to legal, I'd also propose adding an attestation clause (annual) rather than a right to random audits for smaller customers; HealthCore can request audits but they require a scope and notice.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-11T15:28:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: DPA redlines — model training / derivative outputs

Aisha / Karthik — thanks for the notes. Attached is a legal redline (rwd_redline_proposal.docx) that attempts to strike the balance. High-level:
- Acceptable: explicit prohibition on using Customer Content for model training without opt-in.
- We propose: a "Service Improvement" carve-out limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry (definition provided), operational debugging, and safety/abuse prevention.
- We will offer: annual attestation of subprocessor list and a rolling 30-day notice before adding a subprocessor that will process Customer Content. For customers with elevated requirements (enterprise SLA / compliance), we can provide a scoped audit option under NDA.

Key redline excerpt to send to HealthCore (text):
"Provider shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise create persistent model updates ("Training"). Provider may use Aggregated and De-identified Telemetry for the limited purpose of Service Improvement. 
Definitions: 
• "Aggregated and De-identified Telemetry": Telemetry derived from system metrics, performance traces, and usage counters that cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer Content or to attribute such content to a specific Customer.
• "Service Improvement": Non-persistent processes that enhance system reliability, latency, and operational performance; excludes any activity described as Training."

Execution: We can prepare for DocuSign once HealthCore confirms the minor edits. Proposed timeline: internal review today, send redline back to HealthCore EOD, and target signature next week.

— Neha
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@healthcore.com>
To: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@healthcore.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@healthcore.com>
Date: 2027-01-12T14:35:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — model training / derivative outputs

Aisha — thanks for the quick turnaround and for routing Karthik and Neha. We reviewed your proposed paragraph and Neha's excerpt. HealthCore is willing to accept the carve-out for "Aggregated and De-identified Telemetry" with the following minor clarifications: 1) add a short definition to confirm telemetry excludes raw prompt/response text; 2) require quarterly attestation on subprocessor list (instead of annual); and 3) require DocuSign execution with a mutual signature block and a 10-business-day review window after delivery of the final redline.

If Redwood can accept those three items, we will mark the redline as approved and I will prepare the DocuSign envelope. Once I send the DocuSign link we expect a 48-hour turnaround from your side for signature.

On behalf of HealthCore — Sara Klein
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
HealthCore
